tagline: Push-to-talk dictation that lives in your tray.
description: Clean-room rebuild of a BYOK push-to-talk dictation app for Windows and macOS. Widget-first: the tray pill is the app, the window is for settings. Groq Whisper by default, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint supported. Merges the dictation core with the VFlow feature set (transcription log, usage analytics with live cost, WPM, recap notifications, wrap-up) reimplemented fresh. Copyright LaBroi Walton, GPLv3 from commit one, built entirely on LaBroi's personal machine. No code, prose, specs, or assets may be copied from ~/Projects/undertone, ~/Projects/the-peoples-voice-flow, or ~/Projects/OpenWhisp.

stack.hotkeys: uiohook-napi (prebuilt N-API binaries only, npmRebuild false)
stack.packaging: electron-builder (NSIS for Windows, dmg+zip for macOS)

conventions.verify: npm run typecheck, npm run test, and npm run smoke must be green before any commit. Smoke prints SMOKE_RESULT JSON and every subsystem adds a named check.
conventions.stories: Work stories in order. Never set passes true until every acceptance criterion is verified; record how in notes. Stories with needs_human true get built and smoke-verified, then their human step is appended to HANDOFF.md and work continues.
conventions.commits: One commit per story minimum, prefixed with the story id. git pull --rebase before every commit. After changing prd.json run npm run roadmap.
conventions.cleanRoom: Never open or copy from the undertone, the-peoples-voice-flow, or OpenWhisp repos. Concepts yes, artifacts no. If blocked without them, stop and ask LaBroi.
conventions.style: No em dashes or spaced hyphens as clause separators anywhere. Night studio design tokens only, amber reserved for live states. The product name is always lowercase murmur in every user-visible surface, even at sentence start.

Scripts: dev, build, typecheck, test, smoke (placeholder), roadmap (placeholder), dist:mac, dist:win. GPLv3 LICENSE, license field GPL-3.0-only, npmRebuild false.

npm run build produces main, preload, and renderer bundles
npm run typecheck is green
npm run test runs vitest and a seed test passes
LICENSE is GPLv3 and package.json license is GPL-3.0-only

Versions: electron 44, electron-vite 5, vite 7, react 19, typescript 7, vitest 5.

acceptance: npm run roadmap regenerates ROADMAP.md deterministically from prd.json
ROADMAP.md in git always matches a fresh run
Stories render with id, title, and checkbox state

stories.title: Icon and logo generation
stories.description: scripts/gen-icons.js draws the night studio waveform-pill mark programmatically and emits tray icons (idle and recording variants, including macOS template images), app icons (ico, icns, png sizes) into git-ignored build output. Runs on postinstall. No binary assets tracked.
acceptance: Fresh clone + npm install generates every icon the app and builder reference
git ls-files shows no png, ico, icns, or other binary assets
Generation is deterministic (two runs produce identical bytes)
Tray icon reads clearly at 16px and 32px in light and dark trays
stories.notes: Verified 2026-09-05: rm -rf build + npm install regenerates all 18 files via postinstall (9 app png, icns, ico, icon.png, 6 tray variants). git ls-files shows zero binary assets. Three runs produce identical shasums. Visually inspected icon-256 (ink rounded square, amber five-bar waveform) and 32px tray template, both read clean; macOS template recolors for light and dark, tray-light.png covers Windows dark taskbars. Pure Node PNG encoder plus icns and ico packers, zero deps.

stories.title: Smoke harness
stories.description: npm run smoke boots the real app headlessly (windows hidden, providers in mock mode, no mic, no key), initializes every subsystem, prints a single SMOKE_RESULT JSON line with per-check booleans, and exits nonzero on any failure. Later stories each add a named check.
acceptance: npm run smoke exits 0 and prints SMOKE_RESULT with ok true
A forced subsystem failure flips ok to false and the exit code to nonzero
Smoke needs no mic, no network, and no API key
stories.notes: Verified 2026-09-05: npm run smoke boots the real Electron app hidden (MURMUR_SMOKE=1), runs registered checks appReady, settingsWindow, settingsRenderer (preload bridge probed via executeJavaScript), prints SMOKE_RESULT ok true, exit 0. MURMUR_SMOKE_FORCE_FAIL=1 injects a failing check: ok false, exit 1. No mic, network, or key touched; per-check 10s timeout, 60s harness kill switch.

stories.title: Tray shell, single instance, widget-first window
stories.description: Tray (menu bar on macOS) icon with menu: Open Murmur, pause dictation, Quit. Clicking the tray opens the settings window. Single instance lock: a second launch focuses the first. Closing the window hides it, the app lives in the tray. macOS runs without a Dock icon by default with a setting to show it.
acceptance: Smoke check tray reports the tray and window created
Second launch exits immediately and the first instance shows its window
Window close hides the window and the process stays alive
Quit is only offered from the tray menu and exits cleanly
stories.notes: Verified 2026-09-05: smoke checks tray, singleInstanceLock, settingsWindow, and widgetLifecycle (close hides, process survives) all green. Live CLI test: second launch exited in 1s while the first stayed alive and took the handoff. Quit exists only in the tray menu; window close is intercepted and hides. macOS runs menu-bar resident with Dock hidden. Dev builds use an isolated murmur-dev userData so the lock and settings never collide with the installed legacy app (found live: the old Murmur.app held the Murmur lock).

stories.title: Settings store and encrypted key
stories.description: JSON settings in userData with schema defaults, tolerant load (unknown keys preserved, corrupt file backed up and recovered to defaults), and allowlisted IPC getters and setters. The API key is encrypted with Electron safeStorage in its own file, never written to logs, and only a masked form ever reaches a renderer.
acceptance: Unit tests cover defaults, merge, unknown-key preservation, and corrupt-file recovery with backup
Smoke check settings passes
The plaintext key never appears in any log file or renderer payload (grep the userData logs after a smoke run that sets a key)
Key round-trips through safeStorage encrypt and decrypt
stories.notes: Verified 2026-09-05: 18 new unit tests (merge semantics incl. unknown-key preservation, corrupt-file recovery with .bak, atomic saves, keystore round-trip with injected cipher, no-plaintext-on-disk, masked status). Smoke checks settings and secureKey green: real safeStorage round-trip of a probe key then cleared. Leak scan: probe plaintext appears zero times in smoke output, userData tree, or settings.json; key lives only in key.enc encrypted. Renderer receives only {present, masked}.

stories.title: Global hotkeys: hold and toggle
stories.description: uiohook-napi global listener with two modes: hold-to-talk (press starts, release stops) and toggle (tap starts, tap stops). Bindings are configurable in settings with a capture UI that records the pressed combo. Sensible per-platform defaults. Debounced state machine so key repeat and rapid taps never double-fire.
acceptance: Combo parse and format helpers are unit tested
Hold and toggle state machines are unit tested for press, release, repeat, and rapid-tap sequences
Smoke check hotkeys registers and unregisters the listener
Rebinding from the settings UI takes effect without restart
stories.notes: automated criteria verified 2026-09-05 (17 unit tests, smoke hotkeys and hotkeysRebind). Live verified by LaBroi 2026-09-05: captured Ctrl+Alt from the settings UI with no restart and dictated with it end to end. Later hardening: modifier-only chords via code-tracked dispatcher, safe-binding rule (bare typing keys invalid), capture via the global hook with window fallback.

stories.title: Recording pipeline with warm mic
stories.description: A hidden audio renderer captures the mic to 16kHz mono WAV. The stream is pre-armed (warm mic) with a short ring buffer so the first syllable is never clipped. Handles sleep, resume, and device changes by re-arming automatically. Cancel discards audio. Smoke drives the pipeline with a synthetic source.
acceptance: Smoke check recording produces a valid WAV header and nonzero samples from a synthetic source
WAV encoder is unit tested (header fields, sample counts, mono 16k)
Resume and device-change events re-arm the stream without an app restart
Live: LaBroi confirms the first word of a fast press-and-speak is captured
stories.notes: automated criteria verified 2026-09-05: 8 WAV unit tests (encoder header fields, byte lengths, clamping, downsample 48k to 16k, parse rejects garbage). Smoke recording check green 3 consecutive runs: hidden capture window with synthetic oscillator produces valid 16k mono PCM16 WAV with pre-roll included, nonzero peak. Smoke recordingRearm green: main-driven rearm round trip re-arms the graph. powerMonitor resume triggers rearm; a dead track re-arms itself. Found and fixed: sandboxed preloads cannot load shared rollup chunks, channel literals now live inline per preload. Remaining live: first-syllable capture with a real mic (HANDOFF.md).

stories.title: Overlay: waveform pill and live timer
stories.description: Frameless always-on-top overlay at bottom center of the active display: focusable false, click-through, skipTaskbar. The waveform pill renders live mic levels with states idle, recording, processing, inserted, error, plus a fly-in animation and a live elapsed timer while recording.
acceptance: Smoke check overlay asserts focusable false, click-through, always-on-top, and skipTaskbar
State transitions are driven over allowlisted IPC and unit tested as a state machine
Timer ticks while recording and resets between sessions
Live: LaBroi confirms the overlay never steals focus from the target app
stories.notes: automated criteria verified 2026-09-05 (phase machine tests, overlayFlags, overlayBridge, overlayStatesAndTimer smoke, visual QA via capture hook). Live verified by LaBroi 2026-09-05: pill appears during dictation, waveform tracks voice, timer ticks, and insertion into the focused app succeeded, which requires focus never having been stolen. Bonus shipped: selectable waveform styles (bars, speckle dust with edge fade).

stories.title: Transcription provider
stories.description: A provider interface with Groq Whisper as the default implementation, model configurable. Any OpenAI-compatible audio transcriptions endpoint works via base URL, model, and key settings. Timeouts, one retry on network error, and on final failure the WAV is saved to a recovery folder and the overlay shows the error. Audio is never lost.
acceptance: Unit tests with a mocked fetch cover success, 4xx, 5xx, timeout, and the single retry
Smoke check provider passes in mock mode
A failed transcription leaves a playable WAV in userData recovery and surfaces the error state
Live: LaBroi runs one real dictation against Groq with a real key
stories.notes: automated criteria verified 2026-09-05 (9 provider unit tests, recovery tests, provider and dictationLoop smoke). Live verified by LaBroi 2026-09-05: real Groq key saved and connection test green, real dictations transcribed and delivered.

stories.title: Insertion at the cursor
stories.description: Final text lands at the cursor in the focused app: save clipboard, set text, send the platform paste keystroke, restore the clipboard. macOS uses osascript keystroke (no compiled helper), Windows uses a no-compile keystroke path. A copy-only fallback setting exists. Insertion must never steal or shift focus.
acceptance: Clipboard save and restore logic is unit tested, including non-text clipboard content left untouched on failure
Smoke check insertion initializes the platform strategy
Copy-only mode puts the text on the clipboard and skips the keystroke
Live: LaBroi verifies insertion in three real apps per platform without focus loss
stories.notes: automated criteria verified 2026-09-05: 7 unit tests on the pure restore plan (clean restore, empty original, non-text payload untouched, user copy mid-insertion wins) and the platform keystroke builders (osascript cmd+v, powershell SendKeys, null elsewhere). Smoke insertion check runs the copy path end to end and restores the user clipboard; keystrokes are never fired in smoke by design. Paste failure fails open to copied, so text is never lost. Copy-only mode is a setting (insertion.mode). Remaining live: paste into three real apps per platform without focus loss (HANDOFF.md).

stories.title: Silence never inserts text
stories.description: An energy gate (RMS threshold plus minimum voiced duration) short-circuits before upload, and a transcript sanity filter (empty, whitespace, known Whisper hallucination phrases) short-circuits after. Either path shows a quiet no-speech state and inserts nothing.
acceptance: Unit tests: silent buffer, breath noise, and real-speech synthetic buffers classify correctly
Hallucination phrase list is data-driven and tested
Smoke check silence passes
Live: LaBroi holds the hotkey in silence and nothing is inserted
stories.notes: automated criteria verified 2026-09-05: 8 unit tests (pure silence, breath-level noise, speech bursts, one-loud-click rejected by the 200ms voiced minimum; empty, punctuation-only, and known phrases flagged case and punctuation insensitively; real dictations containing a phrase pass). Hallucination list is data-driven in shared/hallucinations.json. Both guards wired into dictationStop (energy gate before upload, sanity filter after) and covered by smoke silenceGuard. Remaining live: hold the hotkey in silence, expect the quiet no speech state (HANDOFF.md).

stories.title: Format spec and shared test vectors
stories.description: shared/format-spec.json defines deterministic formatter rules: filler removal, sentence capitalization, terminal punctuation, spoken punctuation and newline commands, self-correction handling, and a numbers mode. shared/test-vectors.json holds input and expected pairs. A pure-function formatter implements the spec and vitest runs every vector.
acceptance: Every vector in shared/test-vectors.json passes
The formatter is a pure function with no IO
Spec rules are documented inside format-spec.json itself
Adding a vector with an unimplemented rule fails the suite (proving vectors drive behavior)
stories.notes: Verified 2026-09-05: shared/format-spec.json documents every rule and the pipeline order inline; 26 vectors in shared/test-vectors.json all pass through the vector-runner test (fillers, spoken punctuation attach and capitalize, scratch-that sentence scoping, numbers digits and words modes, terminal punctuation, level off and light behavior). Vectors proved they drive behavior during development: two initially failed and forced a pipeline reorder (spoken punctuation before scratch-that). formatTranscript is a pure function wired into dictationStop; smoke dictationLoop now asserts the formatted output lands.

stories.title: Provider and model controls
stories.description: Settings UI over the provider fields that have existed since US-010: swap the speech and cleanup models from Groq suggestions or type any model id, point the base URL at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (OpenAI, a proxy, a local server), and reset to Groq defaults. Values apply on the next dictation with no restart because the transcriber reads settings per call. Requested by LaBroi 2026-09-05.
acceptance: Base URL, speech model, and cleanup model are editable fields; both model fields offer Groq suggestions while accepting any typed id
Edits persist through the settings store and apply to the next dictation without restart
Reset restores the Groq defaults
The connection test exercises whatever base URL and key are configured
stories.notes: Built 2026-09-05: provider panel with base URL, speech model, and cleanup model fields (Groq suggestions via datalist plus free text), commit-on-blur, reset-to-defaults. Typecheck and 114 unit tests green; settings capture screenshot verified the panel renders. Smoke rerun green 2026-09-05 once the session unlocked (the wedge was environmental, confirmed by a minimal Electron probe failing identically). All criteria verified.

stories.title: LLM formatter that fails open
stories.description: Optional cleanup pass through a Groq-hosted chat model (configurable) with levels off, light, and full. Strict system prompt plus output validation: length-ratio bounds, no meta chatter, and dictated instructions are transcribed literally, never obeyed. Any error, timeout, or validation failure returns the deterministic pre-formatted text.
acceptance: Mocked-LLM unit tests: API error, timeout, chatty preamble, refusal, and an embedded instruction like a request to delete text all fail open to the deterministic output
Prompt-injection vectors in shared/test-vectors.json pass (dictations containing instructions come out as literal text)
Smoke check formatter passes in mock mode
Level off skips the LLM entirely
stories.notes: Verified 2026-09-05: 13 unit tests on validatePolish and polishTranscript with mocked fetch (API error, network throw, timeout via AbortController, chatty preamble, refusal, preamble-colon line, quote-wrapper stripping, length drift both directions, obeyed-instruction detection via length guard, malformed body). Three prompt-injection vectors added to shared/test-vectors.json and passing (dictated instructions transcribed literally). Smoke llmFormatter green: clean accepts, chatty and 500 and obeyed all fail open. Wiring: runs only at Full level, never in smoke, never without a key, single attempt with 8s cap, falls back to deterministic output on any failure; off and light skip the LLM entirely. Uses the configured cleanup model and base URL per dictation.

stories.title: Custom dictionary
stories.description: A user dictionary of proper nouns and replacement pairs applied deterministically after transcription and offered to the LLM as hints without leaking. Settings UI lists, adds, edits, and removes entries.
acceptance: Vectors cover replacements, casing of proper nouns, and word-boundary safety
Leak test: a large dictionary plus an unrelated dictation never injects dictionary words into output
Dictionary hint text never appears in inserted output in any mocked-LLM failure mode
Settings UI round-trips entries to the store
stories.notes: Verified 2026-09-05: applyDictionary is pure, word-boundary safe (conditional boundaries so c++ style terms work), case-insensitive in, exact casing out, longest phrase wins, regex-escaped, type-resilient against hand-edited settings. Four shared vectors including brand casing surviving sentence-start capitalization via enforceDictionaryCasing, which runs last in the pipeline. LLM hint via dictionaryHint with a Preferred spellings leak sentinel; hint echo can never reach output (unit tested). Settings UI editor with add and remove. Smoke dictionary check covers replacement, boundary safety, and the store round trip. First story through the independent review gate: reviewer confirmed two real findings (sentence-start casing clobber; wrong-typed entries could throw uncaught, wedging the overlay in processing and losing the dictation), both fixed with tests, and the whole formatting stage now fails open to the raw transcript. 24 dictionary-related unit tests among 154 total.

stories.title: Text expansions
stories.description: Spoken trigger phrases expand to saved snippets after formatting (for example a spoken email trigger inserts the full address). Managed in settings with collision rules: longest trigger wins, one expansion per utterance position.
acceptance: Vectors cover expansion, longest-match collision, and no-match passthrough
Settings UI round-trips expansions to the store
Expansions apply after the formatter so triggers are matched on clean text
stories.notes: Verified 2026-09-05: applyExpansions is single-pass (snippet content never rescanned, so no recursive expansion), longest-trigger-wins at a position, non-overlapping, boundary-safe via the shared matcher, case-insensitive triggers with verbatim snippets, type-resilient. 8 unit tests plus 3 shared vectors (post-formatting trigger match, longest wins, no rescan); vector runner now mirrors the full pipeline order. Settings editor via generalized PairAdd; smoke expansions check covers apply, boundary, and store round trip. Review gate round two: reviewer confirmed the snippet editor could not produce the multi-line sign-offs the feature advertises (fixed with a textarea, Enter for newline, Cmd or Ctrl+Enter submits); its matchAll typing finding was verified not applicable on this toolchain (typecheck green on TS 7) and recorded rather than dropped.

stories.title: History: append-only log and home transcription view
stories.description: Every completed session appends a JSONL event to userData: timestamp, duration, raw text, final text, word count, WPM, and cost estimate. The home view of the settings window is the transcription log grouped by date with copy buttons, live updates as sessions land, a retention setting, and clear-all.
acceptance: Append, read, date grouping, and corrupt-line tolerance are unit tested
Smoke check history writes and reads a synthetic session end to end
The home view updates live when a session completes (IPC event test)
Copy button places the final text on the clipboard, retention prunes old entries, clear-all empties the log
stories.notes: Verified 2026-09-05: append-only JSONL log with corrupt-line tolerance, retention pruning (0 keeps forever), atomic rewrites, clear-all; 10 log and helper unit tests (grouping in local time, DST-safe day boundary, wpm math, shape guard). Home view is the default tab: day-grouped entries with time, words, wpm, per-entry copy via a main-process clipboard handler, live appends, retention select, clear all; visually verified via capture. Smoke history check green. Review gate round three confirmed three findings, all fixed: IPC listener leak on tab switches (preload now returns an unsubscribe, used in effect cleanup), unbounded live-append growth (capped at 500 to match the list handler), and prune running on every settings save (now only on actual retention changes); plus hardening applied so transcript events broadcast only to the settings window, never the overlay or audio windows.

stories.title: Usage analytics and live cost card
stories.description: Aggregations over the event log power an analytics page: minutes dictated, words, sessions, and daily activity chart, plus a monthly usage card with a live cost estimate computed from shared/rates.json. Rates are verified against the provider pricing page and the check date is recorded in the file.
acceptance: Aggregation unit tests cover month boundaries, empty logs, and multi-day ranges
Cost math matches shared/rates.json exactly and rates carry a verified-on date sourced from the provider pricing page
Analytics page renders from a seeded log in smoke
Usage card updates after a new session lands
stories.notes: Verified 2026-09-05: 9 aggregation unit tests (month and today boundaries local-time and DST safe, zero-filled chronological 14-day series, empty log, cost math incl. the Groq 10-second ASR billing minimum, fallback rates, no compounding rounding). Analytics tab renders monthly card with live cost estimate, 14-day chart (cream emphasis, amber stays reserved), lifetime totals; summary computed in main so transcripts never reach the renderer for charts; smoke analytics check green. Review gate CRITICAL catch: the llama cleanup defaults had been decommissioned by Groq on 2026-08-16, confirmed against console.groq.com/docs/deprecations, meaning the cleanup pass had been silently failing open for all users; rates.json, defaults, UI suggestions, and docs repointed to openai/gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b (rates from the primary models page), plus an automatic settings migration for existing profiles. Also fixed per review: per-day minutes rounding no longer compounds (regression test added). Lesson recorded: verify against primary sources, secondary roundups quoted stale tables.

stories.title: Post-session WPM in the overlay
stories.description: When a session completes, the overlay shows a brief WPM chip before fading out, and the WPM lands in the history event.
acceptance: WPM math is unit tested including very short sessions and zero-word results
The chip state is part of the overlay state machine tests
Live: LaBroi sees the WPM chip after a real dictation
stories.notes: automated criteria verified 2026-09-05: wpm carried through the overlay state machine only on inserted (unit tested), chip renders wpm or falls back to inserted, wpm stored per session in the history log since US-017 (math unit tested there). Remaining live: LaBroi sees the chip after a real dictation (HANDOFF.md).

stories.title: Recap notifications and wrap-up page
stories.description: A configurable daily recap time fires a native notification summarizing the day (sessions, minutes, words). Clicking it opens the wrap-up page in the settings window: a day summary view over the event log. A test-notification button fires one immediately.
acceptance: Scheduler time math is unit tested with local-time boundaries
The test button fires a notification in a live run
Smoke check recap validates scheduling and the wrap-up data query without firing UI notifications
Live: LaBroi receives a scheduled recap and lands on wrap-up by clicking it
stories.notes: automated criteria verified 2026-09-06: 9 scheduler unit tests (parse, same-local-day fire time, fires late after sleep, once per day, malformed time never fires). Recap fires via a minute tick with a corrupt-tolerant state file, notification click opens the wrap-up tab, Test button fires without consuming the daily recap, smoke recap check validates math and the wrap-up query with no UI. Wrap-up tab: day stats, best wpm, takes list, live refresh. Review gate confirmed two findings, fixed: the native time input could persist an empty value mid-edit and silently kill the schedule forever while Test masked it (valid-only commits with snap-back now), and the time-saved line could assert a false positive claim on slow sessions (now only renders when genuinely positive). Remaining live: LaBroi receives a scheduled recap and lands on wrap-up by clicking it (HANDOFF.md).

stories.title: Progression engine: BJJ belts and stripes
stories.description: The rank system LaBroi specced 2026-09-05: adult Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu belts, verified against the IBJJF General Graduation System (researched via EXA 2026-09-05). Ladder: no belt, then white, blue, purple, brown, black (four stripes each), black belt degrees 1 to 6, coral red-and-black at 7th, coral red-and-white at 8th, red at 9th; the 10th stays reserved for the pioneers and is unearnable, on purpose. shared/ranks.json encodes every rank with a lifetime-words threshold, a minimum-active-days gate honoring the spirit of IBJJF time-in-grade minimums (2 years at blue, 1.5 at purple, 1 at brown, 3 to 5 per black degree, scaled to app time), and a title. A pure engine computes rank, stripes, progress, and promotion history deterministically from the event log. Balancing lives entirely in the JSON. Founder provision (LaBroi, 2026-09-05): the 10th degree red belt is the Founder belt, held by LaBroi alone, exactly as the real 10th was reserved for the pioneers of the art; every other user tops out at the 9th. v1 recognizes a local founder marker (honor system, like all local ranks); the Phase 2 cloud tier makes it verifiable.
acceptance: shared/ranks.json carries the full adult ladder with words thresholds, active-day minimums, and titles; the 10th degree is present but marked unearnable
The engine is pure: given an event log it returns belt, stripes, degree, progress percentages toward both gates, and dated promotion history
Promotion requires BOTH gates: a words burst without enough active days does not skip a belt
Unit tests cover threshold edges, dual gating, stripe progression, black degrees, coral and red, and the unearnable 10th
The 10th degree renders as the Founder belt with its own title and insignia, granted only by the founder marker; no usage volume can earn it

stories.title: Achievements
stories.description: Data-driven badges in shared/achievements.json evaluated over the event log: first dictation, streaks (3, 7, 30, 100 days), single-day word volumes, night owl and early bird sessions, marathon takes, comeback after a quiet week, lifetime session counts. Unlocks persist with timestamps in userData, fire once, and surface as a notification plus an overlay moment. Adding an achievement is a JSON edit, never a code change.
acceptance: Achievement definitions are data-driven and evaluated deterministically over the log
Unlocks persist with timestamps, never re-fire, and survive restarts
A fresh unlock triggers a notification and an overlay moment
Unit tests cover each condition type, persistence, and no-refire

stories.title: The dojo: unlockable cosmetics
stories.description: Cosmetics only, never function (decided 2026-09-05). A registry maps ranks and achievements to unlockables: overlay waveform styles beyond bars and speckle, overlay accent colors (your current belt color is always among them), settings UI accent themes, tray icon variants, and the wordmark insignia (belt bar, crown at coral and beyond). Locked items stay visible with how-to-earn hints. Selection persists in settings; locked selections are impossible.
acceptance: The unlock registry gates cosmetics by rank or achievement and is data-driven
Locked cosmetics render visibly locked with an earn hint and cannot be selected
At least: one new overlay style, belt accent colors, one UI theme, and the wordmark insignia ship as unlockables
Unit tests cover gating, and smoke covers the registry wiring

stories.title: Journey page and share card
stories.description: A dedicated Journey page: the belt drawn with its stripes, rank title, dual progress bars (words and active days), a rotating dictation equivalent from shared/equivalents.json (approximate famous word counts: The Hobbit, 1984, War and Peace, the Harry Potter series, A Song of Ice and Fire, and more; rotates per app open and is trivially extendable), the achievements grid, and a promotion timeline. A small rank insignia sits by the wordmark across the app. Share card: a locally generated night-studio PNG of belt, title, stats, and badges, exported via save dialog, no network. Real verified profiles are a Phase 2 cloud feature and out of scope here.
acceptance: Journey page renders belt, stripes, title, dual progress, rotating equivalent line, achievements grid, and promotion history
The equivalent line rotates between app opens and comes from shared/equivalents.json
The rank insignia appears by the wordmark and updates on promotion
Share card PNG generates locally with belt, title, stats, and badges, and saves via dialog
Live: LaBroi approves the look of the page and the card

stories.title: First-run onboarding
stories.description: A wizard on first launch: welcome, API key entry with a connection test button, mic permission, hotkey choice with live capture, then a test dictation. Re-runnable from settings. Alongside the wizard, settings keeps a persistent setup checklist (LaBroi spec 2026-09-05): each step shows a green check when complete, the overall setup indicator shows a green check or a red x at a glance, and clicking a failing step scrolls to and highlights the field that needs fixing. Smoke completes the whole wizard in mock mode.
acceptance: Wizard state machine is unit tested including back navigation and abandonment
Smoke completes the wizard end to end in mock mode
The connection test button reports success and failure states from the provider
